lesson_title: Overdrawn to In Credit: One Line of Integers
hook_text: Start the month R250 overdrawn. Salary in, three debit orders out, bank fee. Where do you land? One line.
clip_script: Keep a running balance, one event at a time. Start: overdrawn by R250 — negative 250, you owe the bank. Salary comes in: R1 200. Negative 250 plus 1 200 is 950. Three debit orders of R180 go off — the same thing three times, so 3 times 180, which is 540. 950 minus 540 is 410. Then the bank takes a R45 fee: 410 minus 45 is 365. You end the month with R365, in the black. Written as one line: negative 250 plus 1 200 minus 3 times 180 minus 45. The three debit orders get MULTIPLIED — that is where most of the lost marks hide.
visual_style: A bank balance bar starts red below a zero line, shoots green with the salary, drops three equal steps for the debit orders, nudges down for the fee and settles at 365; the single expression assembles underneath term by term.
pacing: Steady step-by-step walk, with a beat of emphasis on the multiplied debit orders.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and turn any money story into one line you can check.
